articles.title: De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players
articles.dek: De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’ Tuchel hits out at media for ‘creating confusion’ Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in…
articles.description: De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’ Tuchel hits out at media for ‘creating confusion’ Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night. This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004 . And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].” Continue reading...

articles.description: Brazil loss in Singapore marred by unruly end to friendly Argentina beaten 2-1 by Uruguay in Buenos Aires Raphinha was sent off as Brazil crashed to a 3-2 defeat by Japan in their international friendly in Singapore. The Barcelona captain had been substituted after 71 minutes, but was shown a red card after protesting against Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time winner on the touchline. The Brazil head coach, Carlo Ancelotti, was also sent off in a fractious ending to the match. Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinícius Júnior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner. Continue reading...

articles.title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain
articles.dek: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to…
articles.description: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award . Luis de la Fuente , the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be Lamine Yamal , the kid who lifted the Kopa award as the best young player for the third year running and said he would have preferred Pau Cubarsí to be standing there instead. And, yes, Cubarsí will be there too for the final Nations League group game. At 1.45pm on Friday the world and European champions landed back at Madrid’s Barajas airport from Prague, where they had won again, before making their way by bus to their Las Rozas HQ, around the M40 motorway to the north-west of the capital. At about the same time, Lamine Yamal arrived from Barcelona, due in at midday. As was Mikel Oyarzabal , scorer of the winner at Euro 2024 and Spain’s top marksman this summer (not that he would ever tell you so) from San Sebastián. At 7.30pm, they trained, preparing to meet the World Cup semi-finalists and the team they defeated in Berlin at the end of Euro 2024. Two starters from the World Cup final will be absent: Dani Olmo and the captain, 2024 Ballon d’Or winner Rodri , are injured. But everyone else will be there. Continue reading...

articles.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
articles.dek: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come.…
articles.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. Continue reading...

articles.title: Nations League: Germany set up Netherlands clash after beating Serbia
articles.dek: Florian Wirtz on target in Germany’s 3-1 win in Serbia Tijjani Reijnders hat-trick as Netherlands hammer Greece Germany cruised to a 3-1 win against Serbia in Belgrade on…
articles.description: Florian Wirtz on target in Germany’s 3-1 win in Serbia Tijjani Reijnders hat-trick as Netherlands hammer Greece Germany cruised to a 3-1 win against Serbia in Belgrade on Friday, setting up a crucial encounter with the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday to decide who tops Group A2. In teeming rain in an almost empty stadium, Germany forced Serbia’s Srdan Babic into an early own goal with Florian Wirtz and debutant Brajan Gruda also scoring. Babic made up for his blunder with a second-half goal, while Serbia finished with nine men after substitutes Vanja Dragojevic and Andrija Zivkovic were sent off late on. Continue reading...
